title: kate-text: find the matching bracket
summary: matching_bracket returns the offset of the paired bracket. A mismatched nest returns None. Quotes are not brackets. The scan does not know syntax. This packet does not bind a key. It does not add a dependency. Linux CI runs the tests.

lane.reason: The function is pure Rust in kate-text. It does not need a window or the owner's eyes. Linux CI is the test run. Also run cargo check for aarch64-apple-darwin.

definitions.definition: pub fn matching_bracket(buf: &crate::TextBuffer, at: crate::Offset) -> Option<crate::Offset>

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: lib.rs adds mod brackets and re-exports matching_bracket. The pairs are parentheses, square brackets, and curly brackets. If the scalar at `at` is not a bracket and at is greater than 0, test the scalar at at - 1. An offset past the end uses the last scalar when that scalar is a bracket. An opener scans forward. A closer scans backward. A stack tracks nested pairs. A different closer at the same depth returns None. The result is the offset of the matching scalar. Keep each function at cyclomatic complexity 10 or below. Do not add a dependency. A new Rust file starts with the LGPL-2.1-or-later SPDX header. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip.

regression_tests.name: brackets::tests::nested_pair_matches_the_inner_closer
regression_tests.asserts: In (a(b)c) the offset 0 matches 6 and the offset 2 matches 4. The offset 6 matches 0. A caret on b at offset 3 matches 4. A caret on a at offset 1 matches 6.

regression_tests.name: brackets::tests::mismatch_returns_none
regression_tests.asserts: ((] at offset 0 returns None. An offset in text with no bracket returns None. Quotes are not matched.
